title: Curve Sketching: Shape & Asymptotes
summary: The first derivative gives increasing/decreasing behavior and local extrema; the second derivative gives concavity and inflection points. Limits at infinity reveal horizontal asymptotes. Together they let you sketch a function's full graph.

increasing/decreasing.plain: Going up or down as $x$ grows.

concavity.plain: Whether a curve bends up (cup) or down (cap).

second derivative test.plain: Classify a critical point by concavity.

horizontal asymptote.plain: A level the graph approaches far out.

vertical asymptote.plain: A line the graph shoots up/down along.
vertical asymptote.in_class: Where the function → ±∞, often a zero denominator.

limit at infinity.in_class: Compare leading terms of top and bottom for rationals.

concept_sections.heading: Increasing and decreasing
concept_sections.explanation: Where $f'>0$ the function rises; where $f'<0$ it falls. Critical points split the line into intervals to test.
math_steps: Test the sign of $f'$ on each interval.

concept_sections.heading: Concavity and inflection
concept_sections.explanation: $f''>0$ means concave up (holds water), $f''<0$ concave down. Where $f''$ changes sign you get an inflection point.
math_steps: A sign change there is an inflection point.

concept_sections.heading: The second derivative test
concept_sections.explanation: At a critical point, positive concavity makes a valley (local min) and negative concavity a peak (local max). If $f''=0$, the test is inconclusive.

concept_sections.heading: Limits at infinity
concept_sections.explanation: For end behavior, examine $\lim_{x\to\pm\infty}f(x)$. For a rational function compare the degrees of numerator and denominator to find horizontal asymptotes.
math_steps: Equal degrees ⇒ ratio of leading coefficients.
Top smaller ⇒ $y=0$; top bigger ⇒ no horizontal asymptote.

concept_sections.heading: Assembling the sketch
concept_sections.explanation: Combine intercepts, asymptotes, increasing/decreasing, and concavity to draw the graph — the derivatives tell you every feature.

real_world_examples.title: A drug's concentration curve
real_world_examples.scenario: Concentration rises, peaks, then tapers to zero.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The peak is where $f'=0$; the long-run zero is a horizontal asymptote as $t\to\infty$.

real_world_examples.title: Population S-curve
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The inflection point marks fastest growth ($f''=0$); the ceiling is a horizontal asymptote.

real_world_examples.title: Cost per unit at scale
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: End behavior (a horizontal asymptote) shows the minimum achievable average cost.
